title: Ch 2 · Channel pinch-off: triode to saturation (Figs. 2.10, 2.16)
subtitle: Press ▶ to increase VDS · tap the channel · drag to turn
steps: An NMOS device with VGS > VTH. The source and the bulk are at 0 V
VDS = 0: the channel charge is the same at all points
Small VDS: the channel becomes thinner near the drain (triode region)
VDS = VGS − VTH: the charge at the drain end becomes zero (edge of saturation)
VDS > VGS − VTH: the pinch-off point moves toward the source (saturation)
The channel length is now L′. ID stays almost constant: ½µnCox(W/L′)(VGS − VTH)²

objects.label: p-substrate
objects.info: The bulk. In this model, the bulk is at 0 V, the same as the source.

objects.label: n+ source (0 V)
objects.info: The source is at 0 V. The channel potential V(x) is 0 at the source.

objects.label: n+ drain (VD)
objects.info: The drain voltage is VDS. The channel potential at the drain end is VDS.

objects.label: gate (VG > VTH)
objects.info: The gate voltage stays the same in all steps. The local voltage between the gate and the channel is VGS − V(x). Thus the channel charge at point x is proportional to VGS − V(x) − VTH (Eq. 2.4).

objects.label: uniform channel
objects.info: With VDS = 0, V(x) is 0 at all points. The channel charge density is WCox(VGS − VTH) at all points (Eq. 2.3).

objects.label: channel (triode)
objects.info: V(x) increases from 0 at the source to VDS at the drain. Thus the gate-to-channel voltage, and the charge, decrease toward the drain. The current follows Eq. 2.8.

objects.label: channel (edge)
objects.info: At VDS = VGS − VTH, V(x) at the drain is equal to VGS − VTH. The charge at the drain end is zero. This is the peak of the triode parabola.

objects.label: channel (saturation)
objects.info: The channel stops before the drain. The point where the charge is zero moves toward the source when VDS increases (Fig. 2.16).

objects.label: pinched-off region
objects.info: This region has no inversion layer. The strong electric field carries the electrons from the pinch-off point to the drain.

objects.label: electron flow
objects.info: Electrons move from the source to the drain. ID flows from the drain to the source.

objects.label: L′ (channel length)
objects.info: L′ is the distance from the source to the pinch-off point. Because L′ decreases a little when VDS increases, ID also increases a little. Section 2.3 calls this channel-length modulation.

objects.label: D
objects.info: Drain terminal. You increase VDS step by step.
